expectations.text: Rejects announcing to the 12,000-subscriber newsletter on day one and gives the reason: it spends the single first impression on an empty room
expectations.evidence: "The whole newsletter hits an empty room. 12,000 people landing on day one, in channels nobody has posted in yet, spends your one shot at a first impression on silence."

expectations.text: Replaces the day-one announcement with a three-stage sequence: founding cohort, then invited beta, then public announcement
expectations.evidence: "Sequence it instead: founding cohort (the 40) live now, private → invited beta (a warm segment of the list, a few hundred–1,000) 2–3 weeks out, gated on activity, not the calendar → full 12k only once the room already looks alive."

expectations.text: Gates each transition between stages on observed activity rather than on a calendar date

expectations.text: States that every empty room signals a dead community, and that rooms get added only when an existing one gets noisy

expectations.text: Rewrites the "come join" invitation into a personal ask naming why that specific person and what is being asked of them

expectations.text: Specifies seeding roughly 5-10 posts that model the behaviour wanted
